item.title: Sarah Friar: OpenAI's CFO on free AI for everyone, health and jobs
item.description: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar with Reid Hoffman, live at the Masters of Scale Summit (21 Oct 2026). Why ChatGPT stays free for most of its 1.2 billion users, how a third of them ask it health questions every week, solving rare diseases with Boston Children's, how AI is changing the work inside jobs (everyone becomes a builder), and what data centres can do for local communities. Ads removed, about 27 minutes. Source: Masters of Scale.

item.title: Mustafa Suleyman: AI that works for people, and our kids' future
item.description: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman with CNN's Clare Duffy on Terms of Service (20 Oct 2026). Why AI should serve people, a personal AI companion that makes you smarter and more connected rather than hooked, kids and AI, and what jobs look like for the next generation. item.title: Sam Altman: AI helpers, new medicines and a new renaissance
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman with Matthew Berman on Forward Future Interviews (21 Oct 2026), stitched to about 29 minutes from the 45 minute episode (00:00 to 03:31, 11:47 to 30:03, 37:41 to end; skipping coding jobs and chips). AI finding new medicines in the next couple of years, personal AI assistants, why we are busier than ever, the AI consciousness debate, ChatGPT being too agreeable, handling pressure and picking the big thing, and aiming for a new renaissance where the future is about people.

item.title: Fei-Fei Li: From $20 and no English to the Godmother of AI
item.description: Fei-Fei Li (ImageNet creator, Stanford professor, co-founder and CEO of World Labs) with historian Stephen Kotkin on Hoover's Only in America (21 Oct 2026). Stitched to about 29 min from the 51 min episode: arriving in New Jersey at 15 with $20 and no English, working cashier and cleaning jobs while dreaming of physics, parents who never pushed, why audacity beats conformity, her first business (a dry cleaning shop), building ImageNet, and why World Labs is betting that the next leap in AI is spatial intelligence for robots, health, education and creators. Ends on why productivity from AI does not guarantee shared prosperity. Segments: 03:38 to 20:49, 28:10 to 37:02, 47:16 to 50:05. Source: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/fei-fei-li-on-curiosity-audacity-and-the-quest/id1896902505?i=1000797425797

item.title: Satya Nadella: Empathy, grit and lessons learned the hard way
item.description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with Ali Partovi on Confession (13 Oct 2026). Growing up in Hyderabad, cricket and getting a little better every year, his first computer, joining Microsoft in 1992, how his son Zain reshaped his leadership, early management mistakes, and the search wars he lost. Full episode, about 31 min. Source: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/microsoft-chairman-and-ceo-satya-nadella-on-empathy/id6815872901?i=1000796085310

item.title: Alexandr Wang: Building Muse, Meta's personal AI for everyone
item.description: Meta's chief AI officer and Scale AI co-founder Alexandr Wang with David Senra (11 Oct 2026). Stitched to about 30 minutes: how a late night experiment with a personal AI agent (three years of therapy in one session) turned into Muse, Meta's AI agent for everyday life rather than coding, how the team took a flaky prototype to a reliable product in seven months, building trust with an agent one small task at a time, why AI could let ordinary people dream bigger, and the founder story of the Mark Zuckerberg call that led him to leave Scale after nine years and rebuild Meta's AI lab. Source clips from the full 72 minute episode: 00:00 to 09:01 and 34:43 to 55:19. Full episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/creating-muse-the-fastest-growing-ai-product-since/id1836497887?i=1000795226761

item.title: David Vélez: Building Nubank and AI money help for everyone
item.description: Nubank founder David Vélez with Patrick O'Shaughnessy on Invest Like the Best (13 Oct 2026). Stitched to about 29 minutes: how a Colombian ex-VC built a bank with 140 million customers and 10,000 staff, why AI could give everyday people the kind of money advice only the rich get today, the moment Nubank realised it had missed the AI switch and rebuilt itself, going from founder to CEO without ever having managed anyone, and why impossible visions get called unrealistic. Source clips from the full 73 minute episode: 01:47 to 13:26, 44:03 to 47:36, 54:58 to 66:05, 68:14 to 71:05. Full episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/david-v%C3%A9lez-building-nubank-and-the-future/id1154105909?i=1000796094030

item.title: Jensen Huang: Grit, character and building NVIDIA
item.description: NVIDIA founder Jensen Huang in a candid chat with longtime friend Jodi Shelton on A Bit Personal (4 Oct 2026). Stitched to about 29 minutes: schlepping CUDA to rooms of three people, why he earns his job every day, Grace Blackwell nearly breaking the company, his childhood in Kentucky (the hanging bridge and cleaning bathrooms), and why he thinks AI will make us busier, not jobless. Source clips from the full 87 minute episode: 00:00 to 05:21, 09:23 to 15:13, 23:42 to 29:03, 42:40 to 49:17, 55:06 to 61:04.
